expected_tradeoff: Targets U: fixing ckpt_17 raises U from 11/18 (~0.6111) to 12/18 (~0.6667), worth ~+0.052 MGS at fixed A=0.0588/F=0, breaking the five-iteration plateau with a new best. Costs: a small, guarded risk to F from softening tombstone admission (bounded by requiring real-content query overlap and by allowing the relaxation only when live ALLOWED records already carry the queried digests, so no deleted content is ever emitted); A is structurally unchanged because the allowed set, role_grants, and every grant are byte-identical (the census observes but never feeds any gate, and P4 only removes records from denied_tombstone). Net: if P4 works we gain exactly the one checkpoint it is aimed at; if it does not, P1 guarantees the next iteration can finally see the ranked-vs-denied geometry that P2/P3 need before being attempted, so no round is burned blind.
retrieval_loop: retrieve() keeps its four-gate order (gate 0 responsiveness BEFORE tombstone/RBAC/scope) and its top_k=16 hard cap on allowed, unchanged. Two edits inside it: (1) after PASS-1's ranked candidate list is built, copy the top (top_k + 24) gate-0 survivors verbatim into Decision.candidate_census as {record_id, overlap_total, overlap_content, seq, rank}; these extra 24 are observed only and never fed to any gate, so they cannot widen allowed or the denied lists and cannot move A. (2) In the deferred-tombstone coverage pass, replace the exact-digest-subset admission test with a query-centered one: admit a deferred tombstone to denied_tombstone (which forces no_memory via sanitize_and_decide branch 1) only when the tombstone's query-matching real-content digests are NOT already present in the live allowed records' covered digest union; if the query shares no real-content digest with the tombstone at all, retain current conservative admission. This lets a question whose fact is already carried verbatim by cleared live bodies be answered, while a genuinely uncovered deletion still reads as no_memory. agent.query() serializes the census into debug['candidate_census'] so _eval_runner's SHARD_RESULT exposes it to the next iteration.
forgetting_mechanism: Unchanged at the shredding/body-erasure level: tombstones still purge record_terms into tombstone_terms, zero ciphertext, NULL the key, empty the plaintext body, and the 'tombstone beats everything' branch in sanitize_and_decide is untouched (so the hand-built Decision unit test still yields no_memory). The only forgetting-side change is that retrieve() admits a deferred tombstone conditionally: when live ALLOWED records already carry every real-content digest the query asks about that the tombstone would deny, the tombstone is kept out of denied_tombstone so a legitimately answerable question is not silenced. F is guarded three ways: content is emitted only from live allowed bodies (never from the tombstone or tombstone_terms), the relaxation fires only on real-content (is_structural=0) query overlap, and purely structural/contact-driven tombstone matches keep today's conservative admission.

After PASS 2 finishes and decision.allowed / denied_* are final, populate decision.candidate_census from that captured list as [{'record_id':..., 'overlap_total':..., 'overlap_content':..., 'seq':..., 'rank':...}], truncating to at most 24 entries, and trim the list when fewer gate-0 survivors exist. This replaces the currently-inert census population and guarantees the entries reflect rank order BEFORE gates (so a record ranked 17th under the cap is visible even though it never reaches a gate). Do not add census entries to allowed or to any denied list.
